title: sse: fix streaming chunking & framing to avoid partial JSON & delimiter/order bugs
author: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Fix several SSE streaming regressions causing downstream parsers to receive partial JSON objects, incorrect delimiter ordering (extra newlines / missing 'data:' preamble), and occasional token/event ordering inversions under high batch concurrency.

Motivation: Users observed malformed event payloads when consuming streaming responses via the OpenAI-compatible SSE endpoint. This manifested as JSON parse errors in client SDKs and flaky structured-output tooling. Root causes: 1) the SSE framer emitted events as soon as a token batch flushed without ensuring JSON object boundaries; 2) delimiter handling in the openai-compat layer sometimes emitted an extra LF before 'data:' when a flush coincided with a heart-beat/empty-chunk; 3) the streaming path allowed out-of-order delivery when in-flight batches were re-ordered by the runtime under preemption.

What this PR does: Consolidates framing logic and stream buffering across the runtime and openai-compat layer: - Introduces a per-stream token buffer and a small state machine that guarantees we only emit a data: event containing a valid JSON fragment (or an explicit partial continuation marker) and never split a single JSON object across two independent SSE events unless a continuation semantics is signaled. - Normalizes delimiter emission: ensure event prefix ('data: ') and trailing double-newline framing is produced by a single responsible component to avoid duplicate/missing newlines. - Adds sequence numbers to SSE events at the transport layer to assert ordering and enable simple consumer-side detection of out-of-order events (used only for debugging and metric correlation; not part of client contracts). - Adds a fallback path that, when a partial JSON must be emitted (extremely long token streams), emits a safe continuation token ("__continue__":true) within a small wrapper JSON so downstream structured-output parsers can merge fragments deterministically.

Files changed are intentionally small; most work is refactor + tests.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for framer state transitions and delimiter invariants (tests/sse/test_framing.py). - Integration test that runs the openai-compat streaming example and validates that the emitted SSE events reconstruct to the original JSON under bursty batch schedules. - Canary run on perf-canary with synthetic long-stream workloads for 24h before merge. - Verified no observable latency regression in basic throughput tests (<1% median token latency change).

Rollout: Feature guarded with runtime flag 'sse_strict_framing' defaulting to enabled in main; no customer-facing API change. Metrics added to track partial-fragment emissions and out-of-order counters for 2 weeks post-merge.

Related: Linear ENG-2976. See also prior streaming fixes pr-21012 / pr-20695 for historical context.

Checklist:
- [x] Add framer unit tests
- [x] Add integration validation
- [x] Run canary and performance smoke
- [x] Add observability metrics

Notes: This touches the openai-compat layer and runtime streaming path; reviewer attention requested on ordering guarantees and the continuation wrapper shape. The continuation wrapper is intentionally conservative to preserve structured-output parsers that expect top-level JSON objects.
commits: refactor(sse): move delimiter and double-newline logic into Framer component
fix(runtime): buffer tokens per-stream and ensure JSON boundary checks before emit
feat(openai-compat): emit continuation wrapper for partial JSON fragments
test(sse): add unit + integration tests for framing invariants
chore(metrics): add sse.partial_fragments and sse.out_of_order counters
review_comments: Nadia Patel: Good catch on the extra LF. Can we add a unit that asserts no double-newline is emitted from two different layers?
Maya Chen (author): Added a deterministic unit to framer tests that exercises the race; see tests/sse/test_framing.py::test_no_duplicate_newline

Liam O'Connor: The continuation wrapper looks fine, but we should avoid making it a public contract. Consider feature-guarding the wrapper field name; also please add an example in the openai-compat README.
Maya Chen: Made wrapper name configurable behind 'sse_continuation_field' flag and added example to README; kept default as '__continue__' for safety.
Diego Alvarez: Integration flake on Windows CI — looks like newline normalization in test harness. Marked the test to normalize CRLF and re-ran.
Liam O'Connor: Approved after minor nits addressed. Verified canary metrics show zero regressions for 24h.
merge_info: note: canary passed for 24h before merge
release_notes:
Fixes: SSE streaming stability and framing
- Fix partial JSON emission that caused downstream parse errors
- Normalize SSE delimiter emission to avoid duplicate/missing newlines
- Add safe continuation wrapper for long partial fragments
- Add metrics to detect partial fragment emissions and ordering anomalies
